problems.issue: Core features are underreported: speech delay 22% versus 58% in R1-train, macrocephaly 19% versus 39%, developmental delay 20% versus 37%, and hypotonia 13% versus 32%. The resulting records inadequately represent the characteristic neurodevelopmental and macrocephaly phenotype.

Example 1 consists of intellectual disability plus salt craving and decreased CD4+ T-cell proportion, suggesting an unrelated endocrine or immune phenotype. Other examples add pulmonic stenosis or broad hallux while providing little characteristic SETD2 context. Such records could teach misleading disease associations.

Short stature in 22% of reported cases is unexpectedly prominent for Luscan-Lumish syndrome, which typically features overgrowth. Although growth is variable, this frequency warrants checking for phenotype mixing or inappropriate feature sampling.

summary: Age and sex are plausible, but suppression of hallmark findings and prominent unrelated findings make the simulated disease representation implausible. Without literature-panel rows, true-rate calibration cannot be assessed reliably.
